title: Generate Tag for Video Caption
statement:
Turn the video caption `caption` into a hashtag and return it. The words of `caption` are its maximal runs of letters: spaces only separate words, and there may be several spaces in a row or spaces at either end. Build the tag like this:

1. Begin with the character `'#'`.
2. Append the first word with every letter in lowercase.
3. Append each later word in order, with its first letter in uppercase and all of its other letters in lowercase. No spaces are kept.
4. If the result has more than 100 characters, keep only its first 100 (the `'#'` is one of them).

A caption with no words at all gives the tag `"#"`.
constraints: caption contains only English letters (either case) and spaces

tests.name: Test 10
input: abcdefghij abcdefghij abcdefghij abcdefghij abcdefghij abcdefghij abcdefghij abcdefghij abcdefghij abcdefghij abcdefghij abcdefghij abcdefghij

notes:
## Intuition

The tag is just the caption's words glued together. Each letter's case depends only on two things: whether it is the first letter of its word, and whether that word is the first word. Splitting the caption into words turns every rule into a one-liner, and the 100-character limit can be applied once at the very end.

## Approach

1. Split `caption` on spaces and drop the empty pieces that repeated, leading or trailing spaces leave behind; the rest is `words`.
2. Start `tag` as `'#'`.
3. For each index `i`, lowercase the word into `word`. The first word (`i === 0`) is appended as it is; every other word gets its first letter uppercased before it is appended.
4. Return the first 100 characters of `tag` (`slice` returns the whole string when it is shorter).

## Example 1, step by step

`words` is `["Leetcode", "daily", "streak", "achieved"]`. With `i = 0`, `word = "leetcode"` is appended as it is, so `tag = "#leetcode"`. With `i = 1`, `"daily"` becomes `"Daily"` and `tag = "#leetcodeDaily"`. Then `"Streak"` and `"Achieved"` follow, giving `"#leetcodeDailyStreakAchieved"`: 28 characters, so nothing is cut.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n) for n = `caption.length`: splitting, lowercasing and appending touch each character a constant number of times.
- Space: O(n) for `words` and `tag`.

## Pitfalls

- `caption.split(' ')` alone keeps empty strings. With a leading space the "first word" would be `""`, and the real first word would wrongly get a capital letter.
- Lowercase the rest of every word, not only its first letter: `"GO"` must become `"Go"`.
- The first word starts with a lowercase letter even when the caption capitalizes it: `"Leetcode"` becomes `"leetcode"`.
- The `'#'` counts toward the 100 characters, so at most 99 letters survive.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `words` | the caption's non-empty words, in order |
| `tag` | the tag built so far, starting with `'#'` |
| `i` | index of the current word in `words` |
| `word` | the current word in lowercase |

narration.2: Split on single spaces and drop the empty pieces left by repeated, leading or trailing spaces.
narration.3: Every tag starts with the hash sign.
narration.4: Visit the words in order; i tells the first word apart from the rest.
narration.5: Lowercase the whole word first; only its first letter may change back.
narration.7: Yes: the first word goes in entirely in lowercase.
narration.9: Any later word gets an uppercase first letter followed by the lowercase rest.
narration.12: Keep at most 100 characters, counting the hash sign.
